meta_description_en: Letters from Outlet magazine #89: Glenn Atkins on lottery random number generators and Brian Cavers' response detailing ZX Spectrum's RND and timer seeding.
meta_description_ru: Письма читателей журнала Outlet #89: Гленн Аткинс о генераторе чисел для лотереи и ответ Брайана Каверса об особенностях работы RND и таймера ZX Spectrum.
body_en_plain:
January, 1995       Page Reply

 How to write to us...02     -
 Glenn Atkins.........03    05
 Jim Hossack..........09    14
 Brian Cavers.........16     -
 Mike Mee.............18    19
 Donald Pemberton.....20     -
 George Munro.........22    24
 Graham Yeardley......26    27

   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From Glenn Atkins, MIDDX.

First of all may I take this
opportunity to wish all at OUT-
LET a very Merry Christmas and a
Happy (prosperous) New Year. If
it was you who won the Lottery
(`17.8m), I promise not to tell
anybody and could you lend me a
fiver 'till payday!

How are you choosing your
Lottery numbers? (assuming you
are participating). Yes, you've
guessed it, I use my trusty
Spectrum to come up with my
selections. I've written an
unembellished program in Modula-
2 which simply generates 6
random numbers between 1 and 49
and prints them on the screen in
ascending order.

I'll make it better and send it
in if someone hasn't beaten me
to it already.

I must admit that random number
generators are one of my
weaknesses. Do you know any good
ones? The main problem relies on
the fact that it's an 8-bit
machine and any random number
generator written for the
Spectrum will probably repeat
after 65535 numbers seeing as
that is the highest integer that
the humble Spectrum can handle.
Oh well,I might still win anyway
- who knows?

My very best regards to you all,

             Glenn

Brian Cavers to Glenn Atkins


I've been risking an adventurous
quid about once a month on the
Lottery (all I can spare!). No
luck so far but it's fun think-
ing how I would spend a few
million!

Did you remember to make your
program eliminate duplication of
random numbers? I mean, it must
generate six DIFFERENT random
numbers between 1 and 49!

The Spectrum can handle numbers
up to 1.7E+38 with an accuracy
of about 9 and a half digits.The
largest integer it can hold with
accuracy is 4,294,967,295.


However, you are right,the Spec-
trum's built in RND does indeed
repeat itself after 65536 goes!
You can avoid that by using the
RANDOMIZE command, eg...


  FOR N=1 TO 99999999
   RANDOMIZE
   PRINT RND
  NEXT N


I've not tried that but I think
it should avoid repeats because
it keeps reseeding the random
number generator using the timer
at addresses 23672/3/4 and these
keep changing every 50th of a
second.



The following ought to give you
non-repeatable random numbers in
theory. In practice,I wonder? If
you reset and take say, roughly
one minute to load it every week
then occasionally you may take
EXACTLY (within 1/50th of a sec-
ond) the same time to load it
and the timer will hold the same
values!...

 10 RANDOMIZE
 20 DIM A(6)
 30 FOR N = 1 TO 6
 40 LET R=INT(RND * 49) + 1
 50 FOR J = 1 TO N-1
 60 IF R = A(J) THEN GO TO 40
 70 NEXT J
 80 LET A(N) = R
 90 PRINT R
100 NEXT N


I suppose you might try entering
the date to seed RND...

  3 INPUT DATE (eg 25.12.94); D$
  5 D$=D$(TO 2)+D$(4 TO 5)+D$(8)
 10 RANDOMIZE VAL D$

Incidentally, do you know what
the odds are of the previous
week's Lottery numbers coming up
again? The odds are no different
to any other six numbers!

                          Brian

From Jim Hossack, LIVINGSTON



Dear Ron & Brian,


Francis Miles' mathematical par-
adox:"St. Petersburg"(OUTLETTERS
in Issue 85) was a fascinating
exercise in logical deduction.It
reminded me of a much more triv-
ial one that I first encountered
during my service days in W.W.2.


In those days cigarettes cost a
shilling for twenty (about five
pence) so for clarity I'll use
this figure of 5p as the present
price of a  twenty pack...


There was a time, and for all I
know this may still hold, when
Scottish pound notes were valued
at less than their nominal value
south of the border. OK so you
now use coins exclusively but we
still have our own notes and
until recently so did you - and
for the sake of this tale I'll
have to assume you still do!

Well,a certain Scots tobacconist
living near the border (on the
north side) objected to this
practice of discrimination
against his native currency and
so decided to retaliate by
discounting English pound notes
by the same amount, 5p which was
being levied on the Scots curr-
ency.


Therefore, when a cusomer came
into his shop and purchased a
packet of cigarettes proferring
a Scottish pound note, he re-
ceived his pack plus an English
note in change (which, remember,
was worth only 95p in Scotland).

On his next trip south, said
customer then visited a tobacc-
onist on the other side of the
border and repeated the purchase
this time using the English note
and receiving a Scots note(worth
only 95p) as his change. (The
likelihood of these two events
happening consecutively is, of
course, rather low but by
conjuring up literary licence
let's assume they happened as
stated).


The question, of course, is: who
has, in fact, paid for the two
packets of cigarettes since the
customer himself is not out of
pocket?

By extension of our literary
licence, we can imagine the
process repeating almost
indefinitely, raising the same
question in a much more
challenging form, with shades of
the IMF and Black Wednesday in
the background. The scenario
could, of course, take place
across any European border.


I'll leave your readers to think
of an answer to the question
posed above.


Finally, congratulations on
reaching your seventh annivers-
ary - you look set to continue,
at least along the PC path!
Readers would probably be
interested to know how PC sales
are going, if you haven't
already published these figures
and I'm way out of date!.

Keep up the good work!

              Jim

Brian Cavers to Jim Hossack

PC sales are creeping up very,
very slowly. We've only about
300 on our books so far but we
are hampered by lack of funds to
promote the magazine. Take as an
example our tiny advert in PC
PLUS which we've had for four or
five months. It costs about `75
a month and there has been a
poor response. We now find that
their average readership is the
business user primarily so that
may explain it. We are now going
to try PC ANSWERS to see how
that fares.

At least we are moving in the
right direction albeit slowly! I
just wish it would accelerate!


I had to read your Scottish
pound poser a few times to grasp
it but I think the answer is the
Scottish tobacconist is the one
who has paid for the two packs
of cigarettes. After all, if a
Scottish pound note was worth
95p in English currency and an
English pound note was worth `1
then he took 95p off the cust-
omer and gave him `1 back plus
goods worth 5p. He's effectively
giving him `1.05 in exchange for
95p!

If however, the general rate of
exchange in Scottish banks was
to treat the English pound as
95p then I suppose the Treasury
- ie, you and me - lose out!
                          Brian

Brian Cavers to all

Over the years we've accumulated
four different Plus 3's -and ALL
of them have serious faults! Two
of them have failed tv output so
the display is almost unusable.
These machine are really only of
use for duplicating OUTLET which
can be done blind - just pushing
in the disks and pressing a key.
The other two machines both have
drive faults - often the Plus 3
refuses to recognize Drive A. It
is particularly bad when the
machines are "cold" but it does
also happen even when they have
had a chance to warm up!

I've cleaned the drive heads and
checked for loose connections,
so...

I did have a photocopy of the
circuit board showing how to
solder in a connection for a
composite video output which I
am almost certain one of our
readers kindly sent us. This
would be a viable option for the
+3's with bad tv modulators as I
do have a tv with video input.
Unfortunately, the info has been
mislaid(we have it somewhere but
where?). So, if anyone has that
info I'd be grateful if they
could send me a copy!

Has anyone any other ideas that
might help?Maybe the drive could
be taken out of one of the +3's
with bad tv output and put in a
+3 with a bad drive to make one
good one out of two bad ones!
                           Brian

From Mike Mee, CLWYD

Dear Ron & Brian Cavers,

Can you give me a list of the
Spectrum copies of OUTLET that
contain any useful hacking tut-
orials?

    Hear from you soon-ish,

           Mike Mee


Brian Cavers to Mike Mee

Hacking games has not really
been covered much in OUTLET but
by coincidence, we do have a big
list of POKEs coming soon!

                       Brian

From Donald Pemberton, CHESHIRE

Dear Ron & Brian,

I still run a Spectrum +3 with
an additional +D 3.5" drive.This
is coupled to a small tv and I
find it useful to have Microsoft
Works programs running on the PC
and be able to refer to my old
Tasword +3 iles and Masterfile
programs simultaneously on my
original set-up.

I still have one program I run
on Microdrive called Musical
Typewriter(Romantic Robot). This
comes with a flexible cardboard
section with shaped holes to
match the keyboard of the 48K
Spectrum + and is printed so


that the musical notes are laid
out like those on a piano. It
has great limitations but I
still find it useful. I could
possibly transfer the program to
the PC but the cardboard temp-
late can only be used with a 48K
Spectrum +.

Both of these Spectrums have
connections at the back which I
can plug in an amplifier/speaker
which works successfully. My PC,
alas, lacks such sophistication
- or at least I think it does.

My wishes to you both for a very
happy Christmas and every succ-
ess in the new year.

            Donald Pemberton


From George B. Munro

Dear Ron & Brian,

I found AUTOLOAD in OUTLET 88 to
be corrupted and would not MERGE
but I finally managed to get
over this by using the following
by Les Fraser...

1.Take a newly-formatted +D disk
  (not even a system file on it)

2.Copy the corrupt file to it.It
  will now be on the first and
  following file sectors.

3. Enter: LOAD @1,4,1,25000
          POKE 25007,255
          POKE 25008,255
          SAVE @1,4,1,25000


That should remove the AUTORUN
and the program can then be
loaded and LISTed.

Once again, a Merry Christmas to
you both and a Happy and Prosp-
erous New Year.

           Yours aye,

        George B. Munro


Brian Cavers to George Munro

Yes,I too discovered the corrupt
file last month. It worked OK on
the +D but when I came to conv-
ert it for the tape and +3 I had
to MERGE some lines and found
the problem. As I remember, the
corruption was near the end of
the listing.

I was short of time as I had to
get the issue finish quickly so,
I quickly tried a few tricks I
know to get rid of the corrupt-
ion but without success. In the
end I "sealed" it off at the end
of the listing with a few POKEs.
The corruption is still there
but beyond the end of BASIC so
it does no harm.


I could then MERGE in my lines
and produce the tape and +3
versions but I left the +D and
Disciple version alone as they
worked OK! Incidentally, it is
possible to load and list AUTO
LOAD by this method...

Reset so the screen is white.

Type LOAD P1 but don't press
ENTER yet (+3 users can type
LOAD "DISK").

Place a finger of the left hand
over the BREAK key.

Press ENTER.

IMMEDIATELY the screen colour
starts to change press BREAK.
                     Brian

From Graham Yeardley, CAMBRIDGE


Dear Ron,

I would like to follow the mach-
ine code course which run on
from OUTLET EXTRA 1 and,as these
are only available on tape [to
+3 users], is it possible to
transfer the files onto disk?

        Yours sincerely,


        Graham Yeardley

Brian Cavers to Graham Yeardley

You should now have the nine
tapes which Ron has sent you. I
assume you have copied them to a
blank disk and renamed them so
each has a different filename.

Perhaps the easiest way to read
them is to copy the DISK and
CONTENTS file off any recent
OUTLET disk onto the OUTCLASS
disk and then edit the file-
names in line 30.

The filenames must end in ".#"
and must be spaced out to ten
characters before the full stop
if shorter in order to work in
OUTLET (unless you rewrite the
load lines!).
                    Brian.

### ПОЖАЛУЙСТА, ПРИСЫЛАЙТЕ ВАШИ ТЕКСТОВЫЕ ФАЙЛЫ!

Тексты для OUTLETTERS принимаются в любом виде: файлы текстовых процессоров (указывайте, каких именно), печатные или рукописные письма. Однако, ПОЖАЛУЙСТА, по возможности присылайте нам текстовый файл, чтобы ваше письмо не приходилось набирать заново! Удобнее всего нам редактировать файлы Tasword 2 с правым полем, установленным на 32, но мы будем признательны за текстовый файл в ЛЮБОМ формате!

Пожалуйста, укажите, если какие-то части вашего письма вы не хотите публиковать, хотя мы в любом случае действуем на свое усмотрение. Письма также могут быть отредактированы для ясности и сокращения... Пожалуйста, напишите, если вы не против прямой переписки с другими читателями OUTLET, и мы опубликуем ваш полный адрес.

---

### От Glenn Atkins, MIDDX.

Прежде всего, позвольте мне воспользоваться возможностью и поздравить всех в OUTLET с Рождеством и пожелать счастливого (и благополучного) Нового года. Если это вы выиграли в лотерею (£17.8m), обещаю никому не рассказывать — и не одолжите ли мне пятерку до получки!

Как вы выбираете номера для лотереи? (Если вы, конечно, участвуете). Да, вы угадали, я использую свой верный Spectrum для составления комбинаций. Я написал простенькую программу на Modula-2, которая просто генерирует 6 случайных чисел от 1 до 49 и выводит их на экран в порядке возрастания.

1. Возьмите свежеотформатированный диск +D (на котором нет даже системного файла).

```text
LOAD @1,4,1,25000
POKE 25007,255
POKE 25008,255
SAVE @1,4,1,25000
```

Это должно убрать AUTORUN, после чего программу можно будет загрузить и посмотреть через LIST.
